passages.t: Ahaziah, his mother's counsel, and Jehu
passages.happening:
The people of Jerusalem make Ahaziah, Jehoram's youngest son, king, since raiders had killed all the older sons (verse 1). He reigns one year. ‘His mother’s name was Athaliah, the granddaughter of Omri’ (verse 2). ‘Ahaziah also walked in the ways of the house of Ahab, for his mother was his counselor in wickedness’ (verse 3), and Ahab's house were his counselors after his father's death, ‘to his destruction’ (verse 4). He goes to war with Joram of Israel against Hazael at Ramoth-gilead, and visits Joram when he is wounded (verses 5-6).

‘Ahaziah’s downfall came from God when he went to visit Joram’ (verse 7). He goes out with Joram to meet Jehu, ‘whom the LORD had anointed to destroy the house of Ahab’ (verse 7). Jehu kills the princes of Judah, then finds Ahaziah hiding in Samaria, and he is put to death. They bury him, saying, “He is the grandson of Jehoshaphat, who sought the LORD with all his heart” (verse 9). No one is left of Ahaziah's house able to reign.
passages.hearers:
This chapter brings David's line to the edge of extinction. The house of Ahab, joined to Judah by Jehoshaphat's marriage alliance, nearly destroys the house of David from within. Ahaziah reigned about 841 BC, the year of Jehu's coup in the north, which 2 Kings 9 and 10 tell at length: Elisha sent a young prophet to anoint the commander Jehu, and Jehu killed Joram of Israel, Ahaziah of Judah, Jezebel and Ahab's descendants. Hazael of Aram was pressing Israel at Ramoth-gilead. The same year, the Black Obelisk of the Assyrian king Shalmaneser III shows Jehu paying tribute.

An Aramaic inscription found at Tel Dan in the 1990s, usually credited to Hazael, claims the killing of a king of Israel and a king of the house of David. The names are damaged and partly restored; scholars commonly read them as Joram and Ahaziah, and the inscription's claim differs from the Bible's, which gives their deaths to Jehu. It is generally regarded as the earliest securely read reference outside the Bible to the house of David.

Chronicles has Ahaziah captured hiding in Samaria and brought to Jehu; 2 Kings 9 has him wounded while fleeing and dying at Megiddo. Some propose that he fled first to Samaria and was then pursued; others think the accounts preserve different traditions. Counsel, etsah, comes three times: whose counsel a king heeds shows what he is. Athaliah is called the granddaughter of Omri, Ahab's father; the Hebrew says daughter, which often means descendant. Downfall, tevusah, is found only here.
passages.later: Hosea later said, “Name him Jezreel, for soon I will bring the bloodshed of Jezreel upon the house of Jehu” (Hosea 1:4).
passages.hard:
How can the Bible call Jehu's bloody purge a judgment from God?

Jehu's revolt was extraordinarily violent, and the Bible's own judgment of it is complex. Chronicles says the LORD anointed Jehu to destroy Ahab's house, and 2 Kings presents his action as carrying out the judgment Elijah had pronounced on Ahab for the murder of Naboth and the promotion of Baal. Yet the prophet Hosea, a century later, announces that God will punish the house of Jehu for the bloodshed at Jezreel. Interpreters handle the tension in different ways. Some think Hosea condemns Jehu's excess or motives rather than the commission itself; others think Hosea reflects a later prophetic reassessment of the violence. The Bible presents both God's real judgment on Ahab's house and the moral danger of the human agent who carries it out. It does not commend violence as a model for God's people, and these notes do not linger on it.
passages.asks: Ahaziah's mother was his counselor in wickedness, and it led him to ruin. Ask whose counsel shapes you most, and where it is leading. And ask whose counsel you are to someone else.

passages.t: Athaliah's seizure, and one child hidden
passages.happening: ‘When Athaliah the mother of Ahaziah saw that her son was dead, she proceeded to annihilate all the royal heirs of the house of Judah’ (verse 10). But Jehoshabeath, King Jehoram's daughter and the wife of Jehoiada the priest, steals away Ahaziah's son Joash from among the king's sons being murdered, and hides him and his nurse in a bedroom (verse 11). ‘And Joash remained hidden with them in the house of God for six years while Athaliah ruled the land’ (verse 12).
passages.hearers:
Athaliah, Ahab's daughter, seizes the throne of Judah, the only ruler not descended from David to reign in Jerusalem in Kings and Chronicles. The queen mother had real influence at Judah's court, and she used it. Killing possible heirs was a strategy of usurpers across the ancient world.

Jehoshabeath, called Jehosheba in 2 Kings, was King Jehoram's daughter, perhaps by a wife other than Athaliah, and the wife of the high priest Jehoiada. Only Chronicles says she was the priest's wife, which explains how the child could be kept safe in the house of God, with its many side rooms and storerooms. Athaliah acts to destroy; Jehoshabeath acts to save. To hide, satar, is the word the psalms use for God sheltering his people.

Who to notice: the hidden child, Joash. Everything now depends on him. God's promise of a lamp for David hangs by the thinnest thread, and chapter 23 will show it lit again.
passages.later: Second Kings tells the same rescue: ‘She put him and his nurse in a bedroom to hide him from Athaliah, and he was not killed’ (2 Kings 11:2).
passages.asks: One woman's courage kept a promise of God alive. Ask whom God might be asking you to shelter, quietly, while others hold power. And ask what promise of God you have thought was finished, when it may only be hidden.
